name: allocMatrix
title: Allocates an empty vector, matrix or array

origin.description: Allocates a matrix filled with one value, faster than the corresponding function in R.

arguments.name: nrow, ncol
arguments.text: Numerics giving the number of rows and columns. They are coerced with as.integer, which truncates toward zero.

arguments.name: value
arguments.text: A single integer, numeric, or logical value copied into every element. The result uses that storage mode. The default 0 is double.

origin.details: The installed function returns a matrix of the same mode as value. A negative nrow is "Argument 'nrow' is negative". A negative ncol is "negative extents to matrix". Double NA is NA_real_, integer NA is NA_integer_, and logical NA is NA.
origin.value: A matrix with the given number of rows and columns and the storage mode of value.

translation.description: Allocates a matrix filled with one value.

arguments.name: nrow, ncol
arguments.text: Row and column counts. Coerced like R as.integer, truncating toward zero. A Python int in range is that integer. A float out of the 32-bit range becomes integer NA and warns.

arguments.name: value
arguments.text: One value copied into every element. A float is double, an int is integer, and a bool is logical. None is R's bare NA, which is logical. Integer NA is -2147483648. Double NA is nan. The default 0.0 is double. A Python 0 is integer, matching 0L rather than R's bare 0.

translation.details: The fill lives in the Rust crate allocmatrix, ported from matrixStats src/allocMatrix2.c. The result has shape (nrow, ncol), axis 0 for rows and axis 1 for columns. A negative nrow is "Argument 'nrow' is negative". A negative ncol is "negative extents to matrix", because the C source tests nrow twice. A double zero, including -0.0, is stored as +0. Logical values are stored as int32: 1, 0, and -2147483648 for NA. Extra arguments are ignored.
translation.value: A NumPy array of shape (nrow, ncol). float64 for a double value, int32 for an integer or logical value.
translation.example:
import numpy as np
from matrixstats.alloc import allocMatrix

allocMatrix(5, 3, np.nan)
